headline: Passing fees to customers (where allowed)
description: How to build processor fees into prices or surcharges where rules allow—with Stripe and PayPal reverse math, compliance cautions, and customer-friendly framing.

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your country, state, and card-network rules, and on your processor’s acceptable-use terms. Many sellers choose fee-inclusive prices instead. This article is not legal advice—verify current rules before enabling surcharges.

mainEntity.name: How do I pass through Stripe fees mathematically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Charge (desiredNet + 0.30) ÷ (1 − 0.029) for US list Stripe pricing at 2.9% + $0.30. Example: net $100 → about $103.30. Confirm with /tools/stripe-fee-calculator/.
For US Goods & Services at 3.49% + $0.49, charge (desiredNet + 0.49) ÷ (1 − 0.0349). Example: net $100 → about $104.14. Use /tools/paypal-fee-calculator/.

mainEntity.name: Should I show fees as a separate line item?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if allowed and clearly disclosed before payment authorization. Otherwise, include fees in the listed price to avoid checkout surprises and compliance issues.

mainEntity.name: Can I tell customers to use Friends & Family?

acceptedAnswer.text: No for commercial goods and services. F&F can be $0 for eligible personal payments but lacks appropriate commercial protections and can violate policies. Use G&S or another merchant product.
